text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is diagnosed when your blood pressure readings are consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg.
Blood pressure is measured with two numbers:

list.snippet: Systolic (top number): Measures pressure in your arteries when your heart beats.
Diastolic (bottom number): Measures pressure in your arteries when your heart rests between beats.

text_blocks.snippet: According to guidelines from the American Heart Association and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, blood pressure is categorized as follows:

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

list.snippet: Normal: Less than 120 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic
Elevated: 120–129 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic
Stage 1 Hypertension (High Blood Pressure): 130–139 mm Hg systolic or 80–89 mm Hg diastolic
Stage 2 Hypertension (High Blood Pressure): 140 mm Hg or higher systolic or 90 mm Hg or higher diastolic

Severe Hypertension / Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180 mm Hg systolic and/or higher than 120 mm Hg diastolic (If higher than 180/120 mm Hg with symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, or weakness, seek emergency medical care immediately by calling 911).

text_blocks.snippet: If you'd like, let me know:

list.snippet: What your recent blood pressure readings were
Whether you have any other health conditions (like diabetes or heart disease)

text_blocks.snippet: I can help explain what those numbers mean for your health.
